flashcards.q: Trace Microsoft's GenAI platform rebrand history and what the final rename signals.
flashcards.a: Azure AI Studio (GA May 2024) -> Azure AI Foundry (Nov 2024 Ignite) -> Microsoft Foundry (Nov 2025 Ignite). Dropping 'Azure' signals agents are meant to be first-class across the whole Microsoft ecosystem (365, Copilot, Teams), not scoped to Azure as just another cloud service.

flashcards.q: How is Azure OpenAI quota scoped, and what's the RPM-to-TPM relationship?
flashcards.a: Quota is enforced per-region, per-model, per-subscription -- not a global pool. RPM auto-scales proportionally to TPM at roughly 6 RPM per 1,000 TPM assigned (ratio varies by model).

flashcards.q: Explain PTU billing and its break-even point.
flashcards.a: Provisioned Throughput Units bill a fixed hourly rate (~$1/PTU-hour, ~$260/month reserved for GPT-4o-class) regardless of actual token consumption. Break-even against pay-as-you-go typically lands around 150-200 million tokens/month -- below that, PTU pays for idle capacity.

flashcards.q: What are Foundry Agent Service's standout differentiators versus Bedrock AgentCore and Vertex Agent Builder?
flashcards.a: One-click Microsoft Teams deployment and first-party access to GPT-5/OpenAI's frontier model lineup -- available ONLY through Azure/Microsoft Foundry or OpenAI's own API, not through Bedrock or Vertex.

flashcards.q: State the GA dates and standout capability of Bedrock AgentCore and Foundry Agent Service.
flashcards.a: Bedrock AgentCore: GA October 13, 2025, most framework-agnostic, microVM-per-session isolation tuned for ~8hr sessions, episodic memory AT GA. Foundry Agent Service: GA June 16, 2025, deepest MS365/Teams integration, native memory only reached PUBLIC PREVIEW in Q1 2026 -- behind AgentCore.

flashcards.q: What is Vertex AI Agent Builder's standout differentiator?
flashcards.a: Originated the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol and shipped the first managed multi-agent runtime built around it, with the deepest low-code agent-authoring tooling (Agent Development Kit reported 7M+ downloads by Q1 2026).

flashcards.q: Explain AI Search's hybrid search pipeline and the semantic ranker's tier/config gate.
flashcards.a: Hybrid search fuses BM25 keyword scoring with dense vector similarity. Semantic ranking is a separate, optional re-ranking step (cross-encoder-style) applied afterward -- unavailable on Free tier, and must be explicitly configured even on tiers that support it. A pipeline can run true hybrid search while silently missing semantic ranking if that config step is skipped.

flashcards.q: What happens when AI Search's semantic ranker queue fills under high concurrency?
flashcards.a: Requests are REJECTED outright, not gracefully degraded -- the semantic ranker uses an internal queue for concurrent requests, and once it fills, further requests fail rather than falling back silently to non-semantic ranking.

flashcards.q: How does AI Search's vector index quota work?
flashcards.a: It's a memory constraint, scaled PER PARTITION (roughly 35GB per partition for post-April-2024 S1 services). HNSW-indexed vector fields must reside fully in memory during queries; exhaustive KNN fields page into memory dynamically and don't consume vector quota.

flashcards.q: What is an Azure OpenAI 'deployment' and how does it differ from calling OpenAI's own API directly?
flashcards.a: A deployment is a named binding of a specific model version to assigned capacity (TPM or PTU) within an Azure OpenAI resource; API calls reference the deployment name, not the raw model name. This indirection enables per-deployment capacity assignment and content-filter policy, unlike OpenAI's own API which takes the model name directly.

flashcards.q: Why does GPT-5 exclusivity matter architecturally for a cloud-agnostic AI system design, not just commercially?
flashcards.a: A cloud-agnostic abstraction can swap providers offering comparable-tier models, but cannot swap to an equivalent GPT-5 elsewhere since it's Azure/OpenAI-exclusive -- true multi-cloud portability for the absolute frontier model tier doesn't exist, and a good design states this lock-in tradeoff explicitly rather than assuming full provider-agnosticism is free.
